=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml:132, 153-154 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Each Claude probe inherits `ALL_SECRETS_JSON`, exposing every pool token and `GH_PAT` instead of only the token assigned to that probe.
  WHY: The subprocess environment defeats per-account credential isolation and makes all repository secrets accessible to the probe and its child processes.
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml:184-191, 243-248, 267-273, 331-350 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The auto-mode worker can modify the sibling `pool` checkout, then the always-run redaction step executes the redaction helper from that same writable checkout.
  WHY: A prompt-directed replacement of the helper can bypass transcript sanitization before the workflow uploads the transcript artifact.
- scripts/claude_pool.py:696-703 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `redact_text` does not redact plain base64-encoded secrets.
  WHY: An auto-mode worker can print a base64-encoded token that survives redaction and is retained in the transcript artifact.
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml:250 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The MCP config relies on Claude Code expanding the literal `${CLAUDE_POOL_MCP_TOKEN}` at connection time, an undocumented behavior.
  WHY: If that expansion changes, the GitHub MCP receives an invalid bearer token and its calls fail.
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml:243-248, 267-273 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The workflow comment says the deny rule blocks shell redirects to `.claude/**`, but Bash is not denied and auto-mode commands can write there.
  WHY: The comment overstates the protection; severity disagreement: openai_gpt-6-luna rates this MAJOR, while the other reviewers rate it NIT.
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml:63, 153 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The select job's 10-minute timeout can be exceeded by four or more sequential probes, each allowed up to 180 seconds.
  WHY: During slow or degraded API responses, the job can terminate before producing a selection and per-account probe result.
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml:160; scripts/claude_pool.py:414-424 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The probe records passed to `choose` omit reset timestamps, leaving `_usable_at` without the fields needed to determine an account's earliest usable time.
  WHY: The resulting `all_gated` output has `resets_at: null`, contrary to the documented dispatcher contract; minimax_minimax-m3 and z-ai_glm-5_2 explicitly report that this is a false positive because the filtered records are only for logging and `choose` reads the full JSONL records.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: The phase 1 checklist should enumerate the worker script subcommands that the implementation ships, including `config` and `redact`.
  expected_change_site: docs/implement-plan/claude-actions-worker-pool.md phase 1 checklist
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: The checklist names only `accounts`, `normalize`, `probe-parse`, `choose`, `prompt`, `classify`, and `run-name`; `scripts/claude_pool.py` also implements `config` and `redact`. Reviewers disagree whether the PR description's evidence table also omits `redact`.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml, Line or code reference: 132, 152-154 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The probe step exports all repository secrets as `ALL_SECRETS_JSON`, which each probe subprocess inherits.
  WHY: The probe and its child processes can access credentials for every pool account and `GH_PAT`, defeating per-account isolation.
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml, Line or code reference: 246-248, 331-341; scripts/claude_pool.py:689-711 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The auto-mode worker can replace `pool/scripts/claude_pool.py`, which the later redaction step executes.
  WHY: A modified helper can bypass transcript sanitization before the artifact upload.
- scripts/claude_pool.py, Line or code reference: 696-703 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `redact_text` does not include plain base64-encoded secrets in its redaction set.
  WHY: A prompt can direct the worker to print `GH_TOKEN` as plain base64, which survives redaction and is uploaded in the transcript artifact.
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml, Line or code reference: 250 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The MCP config contains literal `${CLAUDE_POOL_MCP_TOKEN}` text produced by a single-quoted jq filter.
  WHY: Worker authentication relies on undocumented Claude Code environment-variable expansion in MCP config values.
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml, Line or code reference: 243-248 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The comment says the deny rule covers shell redirects to `.claude/**`, but the deny list only covers `Edit`, `Write`, and `NotebookEdit`.
  WHY: Bash is auto-approved, so shell redirects are not blocked as the comment claims.
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml, Line or code reference: 63, 149 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The 10-minute select-job timeout can be exceeded by four or more sequential probes with 180-second limits.
  WHY: Slow probes can leave the job without per-account probe data or a more informative verdict.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: Phase 1 checklist in `docs/implement-plan/claude-actions-worker-pool.md` line 17 lists the worker script subcommands as `accounts`, `normalize`, `probe-parse`, `choose`, `prompt`, `classify`, `run-name`. Expected change site: docs/implement-plan/claude-actions-worker-pool.md, phase checklist line 17; and the PR description's phase checklist evidence table. Evidence of absence: The shipped `scripts/claude_pool.py` also implements the `redact` subcommand (lines 862-877 of the script, integrated via AD-4), but `redact` is not listed in the phase checklist or the PR description's evidence table. The code is complete; the documentation entry is stale. Consequence: a reader of the checklist sees 7 subcommands but the script has 8. SEVERITY: NIT ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml, location: line 153 (Probe every pool account step)
  PROBLEM: The probe CLI process inherits `ALL_SECRETS_JSON`, retaining the full secrets payload in its environment.
  WHY: The reviewer recommends `env -u ALL_SECRETS_JSON` as defense-in-depth hygiene, despite the hardcoded prompt and strict MCP config.
- scripts/claude_pool.py, location: line 703 (redact_text function)
  PROBLEM: `redact_text` does not match plain base64-encoded tokens.
  WHY: The reviewer recommends adding the plain base64 form to the redaction candidates.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml, File: .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml; Line or code reference: lines 128-160 (the "Probe every pool account" step) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Every probe inherits `ALL_SECRETS_JSON`, `GH_PAT`, and other pool tokens from the step environment.
  WHY: Probe processes can access credentials for all accounts rather than only the account being probed.
- scripts/claude_pool.py, File: scripts/claude_pool.py; Line or code reference: lines 661-687 (`redact_text`) and .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml lines 331-350 (the "Redact secrets from the transcript" step) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `redact_text` does not include `base64(secret)` among its redaction forms.
  WHY: An auto-mode worker can print a base64 token into the transcript, where it survives redaction and is retained in the artifact.
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml, File: .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml; Line or code reference: lines 177-181, 243-273, 331-350 (`work` job — pool checkout, "Run Claude" with `--permission-mode auto`, and the redaction step) | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The worker can rewrite the sibling `pool` checkout, and the redaction step executes the helper from that checkout.
  WHY: The helper can be replaced with a no-op before the workflow uploads the unsanitized transcript.
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml, File: .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml; Line or code reference: line 250 (the `pool-mcp.json` generation in the "Prepare the worker" step) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The single-quoted jq filter writes `${CLAUDE_POOL_MCP_TOKEN}` literally into the MCP config.
  WHY: If Claude Code stops expanding environment-variable references in MCP config JSON, GitHub MCP authentication fails.
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml, File: .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml; Line or code reference: select job timeout-minutes: 10 (line 63); probe loop `timeout 180` per account (line 149) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The fixed select-job timeout cannot accommodate four or more 180-second probes plus setup time.
  WHY: Slow probes can cause the job to be killed before `choose` runs, producing a `crashed` classification.
- .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml, File: .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml; Line or code reference: lines 243-248 (the "Prepare the worker" step — deny-rule jq filter and the preceding comment) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The comment claims the deny rule blocks shell redirects, but the actual deny list only covers `Edit`, `Write`, and `NotebookEdit`.
  WHY: Bash is auto-approved, so redirects to `.claude/**` are not blocked as the comment claims.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: "scripts/claude_pool.py [new]: accounts, normalize, probe-parse, choose, prompt, classify, run-name" — the phase 1 checklist in docs/implement-plan/claude-actions-worker-pool.md, line 17. Expected change site: docs/implement-plan/claude-actions-worker-pool.md:16-22 (the Phase 1 checklist bullet list). Evidence of absence: The shipped script adds two more subcommands than the checklist names: `config` (scripts/claude_pool.py:746, used by the workflow's config step at .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml:96-122) and `redact` (scripts/claude_pool.py:862, added per auto-decision AD-4 and called from .github/workflows/claude-pool-worker.yml:333-350). The checklist still enumerates only the original 7 subcommands, so the progress log understates what phase 1 actually ships and the agents.md "Config keys" reference to `claude_pool.py config` does not appear in the checklist bullet. The PR description's evidence table does list all 9 (config, accounts, normalize, probe-parse, choose, prompt, run-name, classify, redact), so the doc and the implementation are inconsistent. SEVERITY: NIT ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
